We also estimated distances to 22 Galactic Globular Clusters hosting T2Cs, finding agreement within uncertainties with independent literature estimates. Our results show that metallicity has, at most, a minor impact on T2Cs' pulsation properties and distance scale, supporting their reliability as Population II distance indicators.

papers.title: Comment on the recent claims of H0 measurements with the ZTF DR2 SN Ia sample (arXiv:2610.36051)
papers.abstract: Karchev et al. (2026) derived a value of H0 by combining the ZTF SN Ia DR2 sample with SH0ES calibrator Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia; Riess et al. 2022), used to anchor the SN Ia absolute luminosity. The ZTF SN Ia DR2 dataset (Rigault et al., 2025) is the largest (O(3000)) SN Ia sample to date obtained with a single telescope. However, as emphasized in the data release, the absolute photometric calibration of the survey has not yet been established to the precision required for cosmological inference. The relative photometric zeropoint offset between the SH0ES and ZTF SN Ia DR2 samples, which is fully degenerate with H0, is therefore unknown and cannot be determined from publicly available data. The photometric corrections introduced in Karchev et al. (2026) do not address this global calibration offset. Consequently, their reported H0 determination is not supported by the available calibration information. We nonetheless share the excitement of pursuing state-of-the-art cosmology with ZTF and are actively working toward the release of a fully calibrated dataset

papers.title: Multi-epoch monitoring of the faint northern component in 3C 84 during 2016-2021
papers.abstract: We present the results of multi-epoch very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations of the sub-parsec-scale northern jet component of 3C 84 (known as the N1 component) at 7 mm from 2016 to 2021. The peak position of the N1 component exhibits positional variations of approximately 0.2 mas at a distance of about 2.5 mas from the central radio core (C1) throughout the observation period. Although a linear fit yields a small proper motion of $\mu_{\rm{Dec}}=0.054\pm0.019~\rm{mas}~\rm{yr}^{-1}$, corresponding to an apparent velocity of $\beta_{\rm{app}}=0.062\pm0.021$, this displacement is comparable to the observed positional scatter, and the hypothesis that N1 exhibits systematic motion is not statistically supported. In contrast, the peak flux density varies by approximately a factor of two on timescales of several months. We propose two possible explanations for the observed behavior of N1. One is that N1 is the counterpart of the southern hotspot C3, but its motion has been halted by a collision with a compact and dense cloud along its path; in this case, the flux variability may be caused by changes in the free-free absorption opacity of the non-uniform cloud. The other possibility is that N1 is part of the northern jet that is heavily obscured by foreground free-free absorption and is observed through a gap in the absorbing medium; in this case, the variability may reflect intrinsic changes in the jet and its interaction with a non-uniform ambient medium. These results provide new constraints on the physical origin of N1 and on the circumnuclear environment of 3C 84.

papers.title: GALI Localization of Off-Grid GRB Directions: A Comparison of Rectangular and Triangular Calibration Meshes
papers.abstract: Rapid localization of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) is essential for multi-wavelength and multi-messenger follow-up, but combining wide sky coverage with accurate localization remains challenging. GALI (GAmma-ray burst Localizing Instrument) determines source directions from count-rate modulations caused by internal shadowing in a three-dimensional scintillator array. We investigate a triangular calibration mesh based on an icosphere tessellation of the hemisphere and compare it with the rectangular mesh used previously. The triangular mesh samples the hemisphere more isotropically and gives better interpolation between calibration points. Laboratory measurements with the full-scale GALI detector yield an average angular separation of $0.86^\circ \pm 0.14^\circ$ for random source directions, compared with $1.19^\circ \pm 0.28^\circ$ for the rectangular mesh. Monte Carlo simulations of 50,000 randomly distributed GRBs in realistic low-Earth-orbit background conditions, each with 1000 detected counts, give average angular separations of $1.91^\circ \pm 1.20^\circ$ and $2.73^\circ \pm 2.18^\circ$ for triangular and rectangular meshes, respectively. The better laboratory performance is partly attributed to its approximately 3-4 times higher detected counts. Additional simulations indicate sensitivity from 10 keV to $\sim$1 MeV, with a peak effective area of about 130 cm$^2$ near 100-150 keV. A compact 1U GALI implementation also achieves degree-scale localization in simulations, demonstrating the concept's potential for CubeSat-based GRB and multi-messenger missions.

papers.title: Gravitational Thermodynamicization of Primordial Black Holes: An RVB Residue Formulation of Thermal Formation and Nonequilibrium Evolution
papers.abstract: We establish a controlled, local, and quasi-stationary thermodynamic framework for neutral, nonrotating primordial black holes (PBHs) by combining a local residue prescription with the thermodynamicization of gravitational dynamics. For a nonextremal spherical horizon, we demonstrate that the positive residue of a meromorphic one-form directly determines the inverse Hawking temperature. Applying the first law of thermodynamics recovers the standard Schwarzschild temperature and Bekenstein-Hawking entropy under standard normalization. The resulting entropy defines an off-shell canonical exponent, which reveals that equilibrium thermal production of PBHs is exponentially suppressed in a radiation-dominated universe, thereby confirming that the standard density-perturbation collapse criterion remains the primary formation mechanism. For post-formation evolution, we adopt a detailed-balance mass law, prove the validity of the generalized second law of thermodynamics, and express the evolution dynamics as a free-energy gradient flow where the moving mass acts as an instantaneous evaporation-accretion threshold. Finally, we derive explicit first-order shifts for the temperature, entropy, thermal saddle, and nucleation exponent under small analytic deformations of the residue.

papers.title: FALCON (FERMI-ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN): Cross-matching ALMA Calibrators with Fermi-LAT Blazars
papers.abstract: Blazars are active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets closely aligned with our line of sight, producing Doppler-boosted emission from radio to gamma rays. Millimeter emission near the synchrotron self-absorption turnover probes compact regions at the jet base, yet large statistical studies in this regime remain limited. We construct the FALCON (FERMI--ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN) catalogue, a millimeter-selected blazar sample by cross-matching the ALMA Calibrator Source Catalogue with the Third Data Release of the Fourth LAT AGN Catalog (4LAC-DR3). After removing duplicates, we obtain 949 unique gamma-ray-associated sources, corresponding to approximately 25 % of the 4LAC-DR3 blazar population. For the subset with available redshift measurements, we compute millimeter and gamma-ray luminosities and find a strong, statistically significant correlation that remains robust after accounting for redshift effects. Fermi-detected blazars exhibit systematically flatter millimeter spectral indices than gamma-ray non-detected ALMA calibrators, while the redshift-controlled luminosity correlation becomes progressively weaker from high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lacs toward flat-spectrum radio quasars. These results indicate an intrinsic connection between millimeter and gamma-ray emission, consistent with a common origin in relativistic jets governed by Doppler boosting and time-averaged jet power.

papers.title: Thorium and Europium production in the early Galaxy: Implications for nucleocosmochronology
papers.abstract: The ages of the oldest stellar populations can be investigated through nucleocosmochronology, with the thorium-to-europium abundance ratio providing a promising chronometer. We assess the reliability of log(Th/Eu) as an age indicator by testing whether thorium and europium were co-produced in a constant ratio in metal-poor stars, and evaluate the uncertainties affecting stellar ages. We present new Th and Eu abundance measurements for eight TITANS reference stars observed with UVES at the VLT. Combining these measurements with homogeneous literature samples, we investigate the behaviour of log(Th/Eu) as a function of metallicity. We derive ages adopting a theoretical initial r-process production ratio and assess the effects of observational uncertainties and sample statistics. At low metallicity, the observed Th/Eu ratios show no significant dependence on metallicity after excluding stars with anomalous actinide abundances, supporting broadly uniform Th and Eu co-production in the early Galaxy. The derived ages are consistent with expectations for an old, metal-poor halo population, although individual uncertainties remain substantial. Higher spectral resolution is needed to improve Th measurements, while combining stars in coeval populations can provide additional statistical gains. Nucleocosmochronology offers an independent approach to dating the oldest stellar populations. Homogeneous samples of coeval stars, particularly in globular clusters, observed with future high-resolution multi-object spectrographs could provide stronger constraints on the early formation history of the Milky Way and the age of the Universe.

papers.title: Discovery of the redback pulsar PSR J2053+6905 and multi-epoch optical observations of the system
papers.abstract: Using the Green Bank Telescope, we discovered the 1.68-ms binary pulsar PSR J2053+6905. The discovery resulted from a targeted search for radio pulsations from a redback candidate, previously identified through optical and X-ray observations and spatially coincident with the $\gamma$-ray source 4FGL J2054.2+6904. We report the first results from the pulsar timing, including the spin period, dispersion measure, precisely measured Keplerian binary parameters, and the pulsar mass function. We also found potential evidence of scintillation and long radio eclipses. To constrain the system parameters, we performed multi-epoch time-series photometric observations using the 2.1-m telescope at the Observatorio Astron\'omico Nacional on the Sierra San Pedro M\'artir (Mexico) and the 1.5-m telescope of the Maidanak Astronomical Observatory (Uzbekistan), complemented by time-series optical spectroscopy with the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias. The optical light curves revealed a pronounced asymmetry, as well as significant long-term variations. From the spectra, we derived a radial velocity curve semi-amplitude $K = 337(4)$ km s$^{-1}$. Combining it with the pulsar mass function, we constrained the ratio of pulsar and companion masses to $M_{\rm p}/M_{\rm c} = 7.05(8)$. By fitting the stable segments of the light curves with a symmetric direct heating model, we derived constraints on the component masses ($M_{\rm p} \approx 2.1\ {\rm M}_\odot$ and $M_{\rm c} \approx 0.3\ {\rm M}_\odot$), the Roche lobe filling factor, and the companion's day- and night-side temperatures. The long-term evolution of the light curve profiles is likely driven by the dissipation or migration of a cold stellar spot.

papers.title: Triaxial $$-PIC for resolving Multi-Hit Ambiguity
papers.abstract: The micro pixel chamber ($\mu$-PIC), a type of micro-pattern gaseous detectors (MPGD), features pixel electrodes structured similarly to a sliced proportional counter. Conventionally, $\mu$-PIC electrodes are connected to orthogonal strip electrodes to reduce the number of readout circuits; however, this configuration introduces multi-hit ambiguity when tracing winding tracks or during high-rate operations. A well-known solution to this problem is the adoption of an additional readout axis. To this end, we designed a new electrode structure using Garfield++ simulations and fabricated a triaxial $\mu$-PIC based on through-glass-via (TGV) technology. This triaxial $\mu$-PIC achieved a high gas gain of $1.1\times 10^4$ and the energy resolution of 22\% (FWHM) at 5.9~keV, Furthermore, the false-hit probability was less than 0.78\% at a 95\% confidence level for two clusters separated by a distance of over 3 mm, consistent with Garfield++ predictions. With this triaxial $\mu$-PIC, single avalanche signals are collected from three independent readout strip electrodes (the anode and two cathodes). The charge ratio among these electrodes remains nearly constant at anode:U-cathode:V-cathode=3:2:1. In addition, we successfully achieved an enhanced gain of $3.2\times 10^4$ without increasing the discharge risk by employing an alternative operation mode.

papers.title: A Large-Sample Study of Interstellar Reddening in Galactic Star Clusters
papers.abstract: The interstellar reddening (extinction or absorption) is caused mainly by the dust grains of different sizes and compounds. All astrophysical observations are somehow affected by this effect, depending on the wavelength and location of the observed object. Different methods and techniques have been developed over the last nearly one hundred years to determine the reddening and to map the solar neighbourhood. The members of open clusters are a consistent population of stars formed together with a homogeneous metallicity. Therefore, the reddening can be estimated in a statistical way, avoiding all problems of single stars and spectral-energy-distribution fitting, for example. Other than for most available works, we can also use more massive upper main-sequence stars for the analysis. We used classical colour-colour diagrams (also known as the Q-method) for (B-V), (BP-RP), (U-B), (U-BP), (U-RP), and (U-G) to determine consistent mean reddening values and their errors. The corresponding standard lines for the fitting are independent of the age and metallicity. We determined colour excesses for 5377 Galactic open clusters covering Galactocentric distances from two to twenty kpc, respectively. The derived values were checked with existing dust and extinction maps. In general, we found good agreement. The solar neighbourhood of +-1500 pc shows a very patchy structure of the dust composition. Our results lay the foundations for constructing a new map of the reddening (dust) distribution and estimating clusters' metallicities by isochrone fitting, keeping the distances and reddening values fixed.

papers.title: Rational Orbits and Gravitational-Wave Signatures around a Horndeski Black Hole
papers.abstract: We study equatorial timelike geodesics and associated gravitational-wave (GW) emission for a static Horndeski black hole with secondary scalar hair, characterized by an effective pressure parameter $p_{\mathrm{eff}}$. Using the rational-orbit taxonomy $(z,w,v)$, we analyze the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), marginally bound orbit (MBO), and periodic bound orbits. We find that increasing $p_{\mathrm{eff}}$ systematically shifts orbital radii outward and modifies the rational parameter $q$. Within the test-particle and quadrupole approximations, we estimate GW signals from an extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) system at a luminosity distance of $D_L=8000\,\mathrm{pc}$. The characteristic strains reach $\sim10^{-18}$ in the mHz band, partially overlapping the nominal LISA sensitivity range. These results demonstrate that Horndeski corrections systematically alter strong-field orbital dynamics and GW spectra, offering a phenomenological probe of deviations from general relativity.

papers.title: The Influence of the Inclination of the Accretion Disk in Black Hole X-Ray Binaries on the Energy Spectrum Characteristics
papers.abstract: During the ascending and descending phases of some black hole X-ray binaries(BH XRBs), it was found that the X-ray Eddington ratio ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $) and the photon spectral index $\Gamma$ had an anticorrelation when the X-ray Eddington ratio was less than a specific value, and a positive correlation when it was greater than that value. Moreover, the cross points of the anticorrelation and positive correlation are different for different BH XRBs ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $ of cross point is between $ 0.1 \% $ and $ 10\% $). The reason why the cross points are different for different BH XRBs were still uncertain. So we processed the light curve and energy spectrum of 15 outbursts of eight BH XRBs during their descending phases. We found that for the same BH XRB, the values of the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point are basically consistent for different outburst times. However, for different BH XRBs, there is a positive linear correlation between the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point and the cosine of the accretion disk inclination. Therefore, We think that the geometric effect of the inclination has a significant impact on the evolution of the energy spectrum of the BH XRBs.

papers.title: Can cosmic neutrinos induce a cosmic birefringence signal?
papers.abstract: A coupling of photons to the cosmic neutrino asymmetry current has been proposed to explain the hinted isotropic rotation of CMB polarization. Gauge invariant UV completions require a Kalb-Ramond field that is exactly dual to a massless axion. We show that, in this case, the product of the axion-photon coupling and the axion-neutrino current coupling is fixed by the signal, $g_{a\gamma}/f_\ell=1/\Lambda_*^2$ with $\Lambda_*\simeq10$ TeV. Using $SU(2)_L$ gauge invariance we show that the dual axion couples to electrons as $g_{a\gamma}g_{ae}=m_e/\Lambda_*^2\simeq5\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. This value is excluded by the measured electron magnetic moment combined with light-shining-through-a-wall searches, as well as by stellar evolution. Conserved anomaly-free currents may evade these bounds, but then either a contact interaction among SM fermions excludes the model, or the relic neutrinos decouple from the signal. We conclude that cosmic neutrinos cannot induce a birefringence signal.

papers.title: Probing the Seed Effect of Supermassive Primordial Black Holes with Weak Gravitational Lensing
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of supermassive primordial black holes (PBHs) as a component of dark matter (DM), focusing on their seed effect on large-scale structure formation. In contrast to the Poisson effect associated with the discrete distribution of PBHs, the seed effect arises because PBHs act as early gravitational seeds, accreting surrounding DM and developing dense DM spikes to form dressed PBHs. These structures enhance the matter power spectrum, particularly on small scales. We model their contribution within the halo-model framework under two prescriptions for DM accretion: an optimistic scenario (Case 1) and a conservative scenario (Case 2), which predict different modifications to the 1-halo term. We constrain the PBH abundance using weak-lensing measurements from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3), performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis to derive upper limits on the PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$, as a function of the PBH mass $M_{\rm PBH}$. We find that weak lensing places competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs, with the upper limits on $f_{\rm PBH}$ becoming progressively stronger toward higher PBH masses. Case 1, which predicts more efficient DM accretion and hence a larger enhancement of the matter power spectrum, yields stronger constraints than Case 2; in particular, it excludes $f_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{-4}$ for $M_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{10} M_\odot$. We further forecast the sensitivity of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) using mock weak-lensing data and find that the constraints could improve by approximately two orders of magnitude. Our results establish weak gravitational lensing as a sensitive probe of the seed effect of supermassive PBHs and demonstrate its potential to complement other cosmological and astrophysical searches.

papers.title: The Pristine survey XXXI. A stream offset from the Stream: very metal-poor stellar debris trailing 100$^$ from the LMC-SMC system
papers.abstract: Context: The stellar counterpart to the $200^\circ$-long HI Stream from the Clouds probes their tidally stripped stellar populations and constrains their interaction history and structure before infall into the Milky Way. Aims: We investigate the chemodynamics and possible origin of very metal-poor (VMP; [Fe/H] $<-2$) stars in the stellar Stream, targeting distant red giants selected from the Pristine--Gaia synthetic metallicity catalogue. Methods: We obtained high-resolution Gemini/GHOST spectroscopy of 33 candidate members, deriving radial velocities and metallicities. We combine these data with literature red giant members and assess their association with the Clouds using orbital integrations in a time-dependent Milky Way--LMC potential. We also compare their distribution with collisionless test particles initially placed in a diffuse LMC stellar halo. Results: We identify 12 high-confidence members based on energy and angular momentum: one intermediate metal-poor star ([Fe/H] $\sim-1.6$), ten VMP stars, and one extremely metal-poor (EMP) star ([Fe/H] $<-3$). The new VMP stars trace over $100^\circ$ of the trailing Stream, follow the Clouds' kinematics, and lie $\sim20^\circ$ from both the HI Stream and previously known, more metal-rich debris, suggesting a metallicity-dependent spatial distribution. Combined with the literature, they approximately double the known red giant sample and extend its metallicity range from [Fe/H] $\sim-0.5$ to $-4.3$. Orbital integrations support an association with the Clouds, while test particles reproduce the debris' broad spatial distribution. Conclusions: VMP and EMP stars contribute to the Clouds' tidal debris. They may originate in the extended stellar halos of the LMC or SMC, or in disrupted satellites. Their spatial and kinematic properties can constrain future simulations of the Milky Way--LMC--SMC interaction.

papers.title: The logarithm construction and (super) Weyl anomalies
papers.abstract: We apply the logarithm construction of higher-derivative conformal primary (super) fields proposed by Butter et al. to derive simple Wess-Zumino actions for: (i) Weyl anomalies in arbitrary even dimensions; (ii) $\mathcal{N} =1$ and $\mathcal{N}=2$ super-Weyl anomalies in four dimensions; and (iii) $(p,q)$ super-Weyl anomalies in two dimensions, with $p,q \leq 2$.

papers.title: Violent relaxation in hierarchical stellar systems: pathways toward massive black hole formation in the early Universe
papers.abstract: Massive stellar systems have been detected in the high-redshift Universe via the James Webb Space Telescope using gravitational lensing techniques. Such stellar systems may evolve on short dynamical timescales, despite a formally large 2-body relaxation time. If the stellar system consists of a large number of gravitationally bound clusters, a 2-body relaxation time can be defined for the star clusters in analogy to the 2-body relaxation time for stars, implying a faster evolution determined by the number of stars per cluster. At their formation, clusters will go through a process of "cold collapse" as part of their early, non-collisional, evolution. This phase enhances the mass segregation between the more massive and less massive population of stars. We derive a criteria based on the mass of the two components that determines under which conditions the massive component may even decouple from the cluster itself. Mergers of clusters and multiple mergers on average tend to produce systems with larger cluster radii. For the formation of massive black holes via dense stellar systems, the most promising pathway consists in the cold collapse of a dense massive cluster, after few mergers (or possibly none). In such a cluster with a sufficient number of massive stars, the massive population of stars will dynamically decouple in the central region and go through core collapse, leading to the formation of a central massive object. In the case of multiple mergers, massive but more spatially extended stellar systems will form.

papers.title: Confirming HSC strong lens candidates with DESI Spectroscopy. II. Analysis of 80 galaxy-scale systems with lens redshifts above 0.8
papers.abstract: The total mass distribution of galaxies provides a sensitive probe of the fundamental physical processes governing galaxy evolution, including gas inflow/star formation, AGN/SN feedback, galaxy merging, and the nature of dark matter. State-of-the-art cosmological simulations have therefore made extensive predictions for the evolution of the total-mass density slope. Interestingly, their predictions diverge significantly at high redshift, primarily due to differences in how these key physical mechanisms are implemented. However, measurements of the total-mass structure evolution have been largely confined to low and intermediate redshifts, leaving the regime where model predictions differ most significantly (z>0.8) largely unexplored. In the first paper of this series, we reported the discovery of 84 candidate strong-lens systems with lens redshifts above 0.8. In this work, we perform lens modeling of the 80 galaxy-scale systems to assess their lensing nature. Of these, 71 systems (approximately 90%) exhibit clear lensing features that are well reproduced by our lens models and are therefore classified as secure strong lenses. Another eight systems are classified as probable (5) or possible (3) strong lenses, based on the prominence of their lensing features and the quality of the lens modeling. One system lacking reliable lensing features in current imaging data is classified as a non-lens. Our analysis nearly triples the number of known galaxy-scale strong lenses at z_lens > 0.8, making statistical studies of the total mass structure of high-redshift galaxies possible for the first time. This expanded sample provides an unprecedented opportunity to test the predictions of cosmological simulations and discriminate between competing physical prescriptions.

papers.title: Scale-Invariant Three-Component Dark Matter and Gravitational Wave Signals
papers.abstract: We study a classically scale-invariant extension of the Standard Model (SM) with four new fields in a hidden sector: a complex scalar $S$, two Dirac fermions $\psi^{1,2}$ and the gauge boson $V_\mu$ of a new $U(1)_D$ symmetry. The scalar $S$ couples to the SM through the Higgs portal. We identify regions of parameter space in which $V_\mu$, $\psi^1$ and $\psi^2$ are all stable, giving a three-component dark matter (DM) scenario. The model is classically scale invariant, and the electroweak symmetry breaks because of the loop effects. We impose the observed relic density and current direct detection bounds, and then study the finite temperature effective potential. For a benchmark point, we find a first-order phase transition and compute the resulting gravitational wave (GW) spectrum, which we compare with the projected sensitivities of space-based interferometers. Although the viable parameter space is small, it can be probed by future experiments.

papers.title: Demystifying Graviton Detection
papers.abstract: Detecting single gravitons is possible through the extraction of discrete energy quanta from passing gravitational waves. For decades, this was considered hopeless, with estimates suggesting a detector the size of Jupiter. Here, I explain how these earlier estimates relied on the highly inefficient electron ionization process, while the absorption through the full mass quadrupole of a macroscopic system can bring graviton detection within experimental reach. Operating in the LIGO frequency band solves the challenges of graviton sources and noise suppression, allowing gravitons to be extracted from known passing gravitational waves and detection events to be heralded by classical gravitational-wave observations. Combined with the ability to resolve single energy quanta in macroscopic systems, such as in quantum acoustics, this opens a realistic path toward graviton detection. I also discuss the general limitations of particle detection in establishing an underlying quantum theory, illustrated by an energy-nonconserving semiclassical alternative. Nevertheless, the semiclassical alternative is not standard classical wave physics, and extracting $E=\hbar\omega$ from a passing wave constitutes bona fide particle detection. This opens the way not only to the first detection of individual gravitons, but also to experimentally probing linearized quantum gravity and the graviton counting statistics of gravitational waves.

papers.title: MP-DualNet: A Dual-Branch Deep Learning Approach for Magnetopause Boundary Detection Using Simulated SXI Images
papers.abstract: The Earth's magnetopause is a key boundary governing solar wind-magnetosphere coupling. The Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer (SMILE) mission will provide global soft X-ray imaging of the magnetosphere through solar wind charge exchange (SWCX) emission, offering a new opportunity for remote sensing of magnetopause dynamics. However, the limited field of view (FOV) and variable observation geometry of the Soft X-ray Imager (SXI) pose challenges for reliable magnetopause detection. In this study, we develop MP-DualNet, an end-to-end dual-branch deep learning framework for automated magnetopause detection from simulated SXI observations. The framework jointly performs coarse localization to determine magnetopause visibility and relative position within the FOV, and fine-scale boundary localization through pixel-level segmentation. The model is trained and evaluated using line-of-sight magnetopause envelope maps derived from global hybrid simulations under different solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field conditions. The results demonstrate stable and consistent performance, with a classification accuracy exceeding 0.94 and a segmentation IoU above 0.97. For the test set, the mean absolute angular displacement from the reference boundary was 0.488 degrees. The model maintains robust performance across a wide range of noise levels and generalizes well, as demonstrated by its application to an independent storm event. These results indicate that MP-DualNet provides a reliable and generalizable approach for magnetopause detection in SXI observations, supporting future 3D reconstruction and space weather studies in the context of the SMILE mission.

papers.title: First broadband search for fixed-polarization dark photon dark matter with GigaBREAD
papers.abstract: We present the first search for fixed-polarization dark photon (DP) dark matter in the 44-52$\mu\mathrm{eV}$ mass range, corresponding to 10.7-12.5GHz. GigaBREAD is a room-temperature broadband dish antenna experiment in which DP convert to ordinary photons on a cylindrical metallic emission surface and are focused onto a radio-frequency receiver. Previous searches, including GigaBREAD and several other dish antenna searches, have assumed randomly polarized DP dark matter. However, vector dark matter produced by a misalignment-like mechanism may retain an approximately fixed polarization, leading to sidereal modulation of the detector response as the Earth rotates. We reanalyze the GigaBREAD data using a polarization-matched likelihood that accounts for the time-dependent projection of a fixed DP polarization onto the detector axis. We find no evidence for a fixed-polarization DP signal and set upper limits on the kinetic mixing parameter at the level of $\chi\sim10^{-12}$. These limits are about $20\%$ better than a naive limit obtained by rescaling the previous GigaBREAD limit under the fixed-polarization assumption.

papers.title: Enhancing Gravitational Waves from Global Strings via a First-Order Phase Transition
papers.abstract: We perform the first (3+1)-dimensional lattice simulations of a cosmological first-order phase transition (PT) in which true-vacuum bubbles with random phases nucleate, expand, and collide, producing a network of global strings. We find that the string network enters the scaling regime, and the coefficient of the logarithmic growth is smaller than the value obtained for a second-order PT. From the axion spectrum, we derive the dark-matter relic abundance and the dark-radiation bound from big bang nucleosynthesis on the axion decay constant $f_a$ and mass $m_a$. The ratio of the gravitational wave emission rate to the axion emission rate is found to be about two orders of magnitude larger than in the second-order case, and the resulting gravitational wave spectrum can be probed by pulsar timing arrays as well as by space- and ground-based interferometers.

papers.title: Coordinated Space and Ground Monitoring of Accretion Bursts in a Protoplanetary Disk: MIRI and iSHELL observe the long-term modulation of gas within a small inner disk cavity
papers.abstract: DQ Tau is a TTauri eccentric binary with pulsed accretion bursts regulated by its $\sim 16$-day orbital period. We have monitored this system with seven instruments from ground and space over 40 days. We present results on molecular gas variability from nine JWST-MIRI and nine IRTF-iSHELL epochs over three sequential accretion bursts with accretion luminosity pulses increasing by factors of $\sim 9$-80. A fundamental new measurement from this analysis is the line broadening of CO (from iSHELL) and H$_2$O (from MIRI) lines, which we use to estimate Keplerian radii and their variability in parallel to the line luminosity. This unprecedented dataset clearly shows that the molecular emission does not react like HI and the 5-$\mu$m continuum with each accretion burst: the line luminosity and width of all hot molecular gas tracers decrease over $\sim30$-35 days, consistent with an emitting region decreasing in temperature and mass as it recedes to larger radii within the $\sim 0.2$-0.4 au inner cavity perturbed by the binary. The infrared molecular spectrum of DQ Tau is affected more by disk dynamics then by chemical changes triggered by variable accretion, supporting model expectations for chemical relaxation timescales that are much longer than the duration of these accretion bursts ($\gg 10$ days). The variability observed in all tracers in this study is consistent with a scenario where gas mass builds up near the disk edge to modulate the burst peak intensity and gas density in the inner cavity every $\sim4$-5 orbital periods. The origin of this modulation is still unclear.

papers.title: A Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
papers.abstract: We present a Transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. Given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts quintic B-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1100,80]M$ ($M$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $C^4$ waveforms in time with exact automatic differentiation. The model is pretrained on numerical-relativity (NR) waveforms from the SXS and RIT catalogues together with synthetic NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv5PHM, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on SXS strain data. On 176 held-out SXS waveforms (165 physical systems), it achieves a mean balanced root-mean-square strain error of $0.023$ and a mean detector mismatch at $120\,M_\odot$ of $0.059\%$.

papers.title: Nuclear Atomic Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The matter coincidence, $\Omega_{\rm DM}\simeq5\Omega_b$, suggests a common origin for visible and dark matter (DM). We show that this motivates the study of nuclear atomic DM (naDM), which is composed of $\sim5\,\mathrm{GeV}$ mirror-neutron DM and a subdominant population of mirror elements. We realize naDM in the Mirror Twin Higgs, employing a twin Froggatt--Nielsen mechanism to generate fermion masses and realize spontaneous $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry breaking. However, the low-energy mirror framework is more general and can emerge from other ultraviolet completions. naDM gives rise to a novel two-stage dark acoustic oscillation signature, multiple correlated direct-detection signals, and highly exotic twin astrophysics.

papers.title: Scalar perturbations in two-scalar-field warm inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar perturbations in a two-scalar-field cosmological model unifying warm inflation, dark matter, and dark energy. The inflaton is noncanonically coupled to a second scalar field that acts as dark energy at late times. Assuming negligible dissipation and perturbations of the dark-energy field, we derive the linear scalar perturbations in a gauge-ready form, including quantum and thermal noise in the inflaton sector and stochastic fluctuations of the energy transfer to radiation. We numerically solve the coupled perturbation system using a Fokker-Planck formalism and compute the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ for dissipation coefficients scaling as $T^p$ with $p=-1,\, 1$ and $3$. For $p=-1$, we find scenarios compatible with current CMB observations in both the weak and strong dissipative regimes, while the explored scenarios with $p=1$ and $3$ are outside the observationally supported regions. Compared with standard single-field warm inflation, the two-scalar-field model yields a systematically larger spectral index for a given tensor-to-scalar ratio.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Coupling Photoionization & Multi-Frequency Radiation Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We use machine learning (ML) to couple photoionization microphysics to radiation hydrodynamic simulations of line-driven winds. ML models are trained on outputs from the photoionization code XSTAR to predict the line-driving force multiplier as a function of gas ionization, optical depth, and the blackbody temperature of the irradiating spectral energy distribution (SED). We implement the trained models within Athena++, enabling rapid runtime evaluation of the radiative acceleration without directly solving the photoionization problem during the hydrodynamic evolution. We find that random forest models provide the highest accuracy and reproduce the force multipliers over a three-dimensional parameter space more accurately, and with less training data, than traditional precomputed tables using trilinear interpolation. Because the framework treats the force multiplier as a function of the evolving local SED, it can be generalized to more complex radiation fields and arbitrary spectral shapes. More broadly, this work demonstrates how ML can serve as a computational framework for embedding expensive microphysical calculations within large-scale dynamical simulations.

papers.title: Detection of Differential Chromatic Refraction with LSST Camera data
papers.abstract: The Earth's atmosphere acts like a prism, deflecting blue light towards the zenith more than red light. Airmass-dependent changes in astrometry can therefore be used to infer additional information about the wavelength distribution of light within a photometric passband. The Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will observe each point in the southern sky several hundred times, with observations spread across a range of airmasses. Using commissioning data from the LSST camera released in LSST Data Preview 2, we report the detection of this differential chromatic refraction (DCR) effect in observations of galaxies and quasars in the COSMOS field. We show how information from DCR can complement the six-band colour information from LSST and help break degeneracies when selecting extragalactic samples and estimating their photometric redshifts. DCR will be a valuable resource for scientific studies and care should be taken not to remove useful DCR information from future LSST data releases.

papers.title: Reanalysis of GW170817 and GW190425 under the Goldilocks Prior
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from binary neutron star mergers encode the properties of the densest matter in the universe, but recovering them accurately requires controlling biases introduced by the inference framework. The recently developed Goldilocks Prior incorporates correlations predicted by a large ensemble of candidate equations of state and broadens them according to the expected detector sensitivity. We apply this framework to GW170817 and GW190425 and find that the inferred component tidal deformabilities differ substantially from standard analyses. For GW170817, we infer both neutron stars to be more tidally deformable than previously reported, with the most probable value for the lighter star nearly doubling from $\Lambda_2\simeq215$ to $\Lambda_2\simeq443$ relative to the uniform-prior analysis. For GW190425, the Goldilocks Prior considerably reduces the range of allowed tidal deformabilities. We propagate the resulting event likelihoods to the dense matter equation of state using two complementary hierarchical methods, a strongly parametrized spectral representation and a broader semi-parametric Gaussian-process ensemble. For GW170817, both prior treatments yield consistent EoS constraints despite substantial differences in the inferred properties of the individual neutron stars. For GW190425, however, the EoS constraints differ beyond numerical scatter even after removing the source-level priors, showing that prior choice affects likelihood recovery for low-SNR events. The joint EoS constraints nevertheless remain largely unchanged because GW170817 dominates the inference.

papers.title: The Goldilocks Prior: Physically Consistent Inference of Neutron Star Properties from Gravitational Wave Observations
papers.abstract: Gravitational wave observations of neutron star mergers provide a unique window into the interiors of neutron stars, probing dense matter from microscopic nuclear interactions to the macroscopic structure, including their maximum mass, beyond which the remnant collapses to a black hole. Accurate inference of these properties is crucial, as many astrophysical, nuclear, and multimessenger studies rely on gravitational wave constraints. Studies on estimating neutron-star properties from gravitational waves often employ priors that neglect correlations between parameters, or treat tidal degrees of freedom inconsistently, leading to biases in inferred neutron-star properties. We introduce a novel physically informed prior, Goldilocks Prior, that is informed by a broad, semi-parametric ensemble of equations of state, accounts for the joint correlations among the chirp mass, mass ratio, and both tidal deformability parameters, and is tailored to detector sensitivity. Using several mock binary neutron star merger simulations spanning symmetric and asymmetric masses, spinning and non-spinning systems, and a range of signal-to-noise ratios, we show that Goldilocks Prior consistently reduces biases in the inferred tidal posteriors relative to uniform and previously proposed EoS-informed priors. This framework provides a robust, systematic approach for neutron star parameter estimation, enabling more reliable inference for both current and future gravitational wave observations.

papers.title: Convection in the interior of Cepheid variable stars
papers.abstract: This paper is associated with a poster winner of a 2025 American Physical Society's Division of Fluid Dynamics (DFD) Gallery of Fluid Motion Award for work presented at the DFD Gallery of Fluid Motion. The original poster is available online at the Gallery of Fluid Motion, https://doi.org/10.1103/APS.DFD.2025.GFM.P005.

papers.title: Stars Within Stars: The Interplay Between Main-Sequence Stars and Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Asymmetric dark matter may form self-gravitating macroscopic structures called dark stars if its microscopic properties give rise to sufficient effective pressure to counteract gravity. We study low-mass baryonic stars embedded within such dark stars, treating the baryonic and dark components as two gravitating fluids. The dark sector is assumed to be non-luminous and to interact with the baryonic star only through gravity, while the baryonic structure is computed using a realistic equation of state, opacity tables, and proton-proton-chain energy production. We find that the additional gravitational potential increases the luminosity at fixed baryonic mass, as the baryons must reach higher temperatures to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium. This lowers the minimum baryonic mass for hydrogen-burning configurations below the standard value of $\sim0.085M_\odot$. The resulting increase in luminosity can reduce the estimated main-sequence lifetime significantly, bringing low-mass configurations that would otherwise remain on the main sequence for hundreds of Gyr to cosmologically relevant timescales. We further show that photons escaping from the stellar surface undergo gravitational redshift determined by the global dark matter mass distribution. Consequently, extended dark star configurations can produce distinct observational signatures even when their outer regions have little effect on the intrinsic baryonic stellar structure, providing a potential probe of otherwise hidden dark structures.

papers.title: On the importance of medium-resolution continuum spectroscopy for JWST's extragalactic legacy
papers.abstract: We argue for a significant investment of JWST time into an extremely deep medium-resolution NIRSpec MSA survey targeting a large, representative sample of high-redshift $(z>1.5)$ galaxies, specifically intended to obtain high-SNR continuum detections. This is only possible with JWST, and no planned future instrumentation has similar capabilities, meaning that obtaining such observations with JWST must be urgently prioritised. The vast majority of existing archival NIRSpec observations are not deep enough for continuum science, being focused on the detection of emission lines. Deeper continuum data opens up the ability to constrain a much wider range of key galaxy physical parameters, including stellar population ages and metallicities, stellar kinematics and neutral gas physical properties, inflows and outflows. Such measurements will provide crucial insight into quenching physics, galaxy dynamical masses, merger histories, pristine early star-formation, reionization and the physics of Little Red Dots, as well as enabling all of the emission-line science that can be achieved with shallower observations. To facilitate future survey planning, we present an empirically derived relationship between rest-optical continuum SNR in JWST NIRSpec medium-resolution data, rest-optical apparent magnitude and exposure time, which we show to be independent of redshift (and hence the grating used). We then provide a 1000-hour sketch survey plan based on achieving the continuum SNR $=20$/pixel necessary to constrain key physical properties and scaling relations for a large galaxy sample at $z>1.5$. We finally discuss NIRSpec sky subtraction strategies, which are of critical importance for continuum SNR.

papers.title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: The Tully-Fisher Relation at $z = 4-6$
papers.abstract: The Tully-Fisher relation provides a fundamental link between galaxy mass and their kinematics. Although its evolution is relatively well constrained up to cosmic noon, observational probes at higher redshifts remain scarce. In this work, we investigate the stellar and baryonic Tully-Fisher relations (TFRs) at $z=4-6$ by analyzing JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of 18 main-sequence star-forming galaxies belonging to the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST survey. We apply a morpho-kinematic disk classification scheme, finding five disk-like galaxies and a survey disk fraction of $0.28\pm0.11$. These disk galaxies span stellar masses of $10^{9.5-10.5}\,M_\odot$, intrinsic rotational velocities of $91-127\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and intrinsic velocity dispersions of $66-129\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. For both versions of the TFR, we find that the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST disks lie below the local relations and are likely offset from those reported at cosmic noon ($z\approx2.3$). By fixing the TFR slope to the $z=0$ value, we measure zero-point offsets for the stellar-mass TFR of $-0.96\pm0.18$ dex and $-0.50\pm0.18$ dex relative to the local Universe and cosmic noon, respectively. For the baryonic TFR, we find zero-point offsets of $-0.57\pm0.20$ dex and $-0.30\pm0.20$ dex with respect to the local Universe and cosmic noon relations. Our measurements are consistent with the redshift evolution of the zero-points of both TFRs being driven by the evolution of dark matter halo properties with cosmic time, modulated by a reduced contribution of dark matter to the dynamical mass on the galaxy scale.

papers.title: Viable Phantom Crossing in Softly Broken Shift Symmetric Gravity
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a viable fit to current cosmological data from a simple Horndeski modified gravity theory that softly breaks shift symmetry. This SBSS model crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$ at $z\approx0.5$ and fits observational data (baryon acoustic oscillations and supernova distances, and cosmic microwave background power spectra) better than $w_0w_a$CDM, by $\Delta\chi^2\approx-3$ for the same number of effective parameters, while providing a physical foundation for cosmic acceleration. The theory is healthy, has no cosmological constant or potential, and has substantial protection against high energy quantum loop corrections.

papers.title: The JWST Early Release Science Program for Direct Observations of Exoplanetary Systems IX: A Multi-Wavelength Framework for Source Characterization in JWST Coronagraphic Imaging of the HIP 65426 System
papers.abstract: We present an updated analysis of the JWST coronagraphic imaging data of the HIP 65426 system. We aim to search for and characterize potential planetary companions as well as provide updated astrometry and photometry for the known exoplanet HIP 65426 b following updates to the JWST and spaceKLIP pipelines. Our measured photometry and astrometry show significant differences to those in Carter et al. (2023) but are consistent to within $2.2{\sigma}$ in separation, $1.5{\sigma}$ in position angle, and $3.7{\sigma}$ in flux. Our results indicate that pipeline updates have changed the photometry and astrometry significantly in some filters, especially in terms of observed flux. We see the greatest changes in separation in F444W and F1550C, position angle in F250M, and flux in F250M, F300M, F410M, F1140C, and F1550C. The SED of HIP 65426 b remains consistent with a young, giant planet best fit by models with a cloudy atmosphere and an effective temperature estimate of ~1436 K. Using both NIRCam and MIRI data, we identified 21 candidate companion sources in addition to the known planet. Of the 21 sources, 13 were attributed to astrophysical sources with eight background stars, four galaxies, one unknown, and zero planets. While one of these sources was detected in Chauvin et al. (2017), the remaining point sources were undetected in previous ground-based observations, which makes this work an initial epoch of astrometry for these objects. One galaxy in particular appears as a point source in MIRI but is highly extended in NIRCam and exposes a potential drawback to single-epoch MIRI imaging in a blind search for companions.

papers.title: Breaking dark degeneracies in $k$-essence models with redshift-space distortions
papers.abstract: Dynamical dark energy models are often difficult to constrain with background observations alone due to parameter degeneracies. This is especially true when the dark energy sector evolves through an effective pressureless matter phase, leading to degeneracies between the model parameters and the matter density parameter. In this work, we show that redshift-space distortion (RSD) measurements help break this degeneracy when combined with expansion history probes including Pantheon$^{+}$ supernovae and DESI DR2 BAO measurements. We demonstrate this in the ghost and dilatonic ghost condensate $k$-essence models, restricting the observational analysis to physically admissible solutions by imposing the absence of ghosts and gradient instabilities. Given the small scalar sound speeds in these models, we also explicitly check the validity of the quasi-static approximation used in the growth analysis. Our results show that combining growth-rate data with stability requirements and standard background observations provides a fast and efficient way to constrain potentially degenerate dark sector models. Lastly, we discuss the matter clustering constraints on these models in light of the recent $S_8$ discrepancies.

papers.title: A multi-epoch VLBI study of compact symmetric objects as contaminants in the search for milli-lenses
papers.abstract: The Lambda Cold Dark Matter model predicts a high abundance of low-mass dark matter halos, which can be probed through milliarcsecond-scale gravitational lensing (milli-lensing) of background radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The Search for MIlli-LEnses (SMILE) project aims to find these rare systems with Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI). However, compact symmetric objects (CSOs) can closely resemble milli-lenses in VLBI images and are the main contaminant in such searches. We aim to determine the nature of the nine remaining milli-lens candidates of the SMILE pilot study and to characterize their physical properties. We analyzed all available multi-epoch, multi-frequency archival VLBI data, new HSA and EVN observations, and single-dish and connected-element interferometer measurements. We tested the lensing hypothesis through the morphology and spectra of the sources, and characterized their kinematics, spatially resolved spectral indices, magnetic fields, and integrated spectra, using synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) and free-free absorption (FFA) models. We identify eight of the nine candidates as CSOs, four of them for the first time. Spectral index asymmetries between components and previously undetected emission connecting them rule out the lensing hypothesis. Only J0923-3435 remains ambiguous. For the CSOs with known redshifts, the lobes have equipartition magnetic fields of $\sim$20-320 mG and projected separations of $\sim$60-240 pc, and show no measurable expansion, implying kinematic ages of at least $\sim$50-950 yr. The integrated spectra of J0210-2213 and J2347-1856 favor an inhomogeneous external free-free absorber over homogeneous and inhomogeneous SSA models. Since CSOs will be the main contaminant in the full SMILE survey, applying this framework will provide the same constraints for a much larger sample of compact radio-loud AGNs.

papers.title: AGN Archaeology: A Systematic Search for Fading AGN in MaNGA
papers.abstract: Active galactic nuclei (AGN) vary on broad timescales, but are primarily thought to "flicker" on and off during episodes of high and low accretion. Supermassive black holes (SMBHs) which are actively accreting material often show optical spectra dominated by AGN emission in their nuclei and beyond. In this work we develop an empirical model to quantify the fractional AGN contribution to optical spectra using the Baldwin-Phillips-Terlevich (BPT) emission line diagnostic diagram. We leverage this model against integral field unit (IFU) data from the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory (MaNGA) survey to select 34 galaxies with weak nuclear AGN activity relative to their AGN signatures at large radii; this signifies past AGN activity which is fading with time (i.e., fading-AGN). The majority of our fading-AGN reside in edge-on systems undergoing minor mergers. We construct a simple model consisting of a disk galaxy with ionization cones and find that the orientation of such a system will impact its BPT classification in both single-fiber and IFU observations. The mean distance to the extended AGN emission in our sample corresponds to a light-travel time of $1.1\times10^4$ years. We use this to set a lower-limit on the typical lifetime of the AGN phase ($t_{\text{AGN}}>1.3\times10^5$ years) which is consistent with SMBHs growing via brief accretion bursts. These fading-AGN allow us to probe the elusive period of post-AGN galaxy evolution, and they give a $\sim10^4$ year baseline for understanding the accretion history in these systems.

papers.title: Why a Multi-Cycle Treasury Program is Essential to Maximize JWST's Scientific Contributions to Galaxy Formation
papers.abstract: The Genesis Initiative is an extragalactic community-wide effort to coordinate white papers in response to the STScI Multi-Cycle Treasury (MCT) concept call. Two of JWST's primary science goals are to discover and characterize the first stars and galaxies, and to understand how they evolved into the galaxies we see today - questions whose fundamental importance has been affirmed by the past three decadal surveys. JWST's first five years have surpassed expectations, revealing a bounty of unexpected discoveries about the early universe. Yet these discoveries have raised as many questions as they have answered, and key mission goals remain unmet. Transforming this excitement into a quantitative physical understanding of early galaxy formation requires a uniform, statistically controlled legacy dataset that the current portfolio of smaller, heterogeneous programs cannot provide. The history of the Hubble Space Telescope offers a clear precedent. Its most transformative extragalactic results came from large, coordinated surveys far exceeding what the standard time-allocation process typically approves, and these uniform datasets remain scientifically productive decades later. We argue that JWST is now poised for the same leap. Answering the field's central open questions demands coordinated, community-led surveys of ~1000-2000 hr, with uniform and well-characterized selection functions that are structurally impossible within single-cycle programs. Such an investment is time-critical while JWST's instruments remain at peak performance, and would maximize synergy with ALMA, Euclid, Roman, Rubin, and future facilities. We therefore urge STScI to open a MCT channel, enabling the bold, ambitious surveys needed to understand how galaxies evolve from first light to the present day.
authors: Nuno Miguel Andrez de Oliveira Covas (IA Lisbon)

papers.title: The obscured nucleus of NGC3256 S. I. Anisotropic AGN near-IR radiation field traced by CO v=1-0 with JWST/NIRSpec
papers.abstract: The southern nucleus of NGC3256, a nearby luminous infrared (IR) interacting system (d=40 Mpc; L(IR)=10^11.6 Lsun), hosts a deeply obscured low-luminosity active galactic nucleus (AGN) associated with a massive and fast bipolar collimated molecular outflow. JWST/NIRSpec observations revealed bright spatially resolved ro-vibrational CO v=1-0 4.67um emission at the base of this molecular outflow extending out to ~300pc, which is excited by the ~4.7um IR radiation from the southern dusty core. Using Monte Carlo radiative transfer (MCRT) models, we analyzed the CO v=1-0 band emission to determine the intensity of the ~4.7um IR radiation field across the outflow base. We find that the core spectral luminosity density at ~4.7um, as seen by the material in the outflow base, is ~2-4 times higher than that inferred along our line of sight, indicating an anisotropic near-IR radiation field. Moreover, the slower than d^-2 decrease of the near-IR flux density across the outflow base suggests a collimated radiation field, for which we estimate a small half-opening angle (15-20deg) and a diameter of the collimating structure of 15 +- 5 pc. This is slightly smaller than the diameter of the obscuring envelope (25 +- 5 pc). Combined with the expansion of this obscuring envelope, traced by the blueshifted CO v=1-0 absorption toward the nucleus, this suggests that the AGN is beginning to clear its environment. We estimate N_H~10^22-23 cm^-2 for NGC 3256 S, which is similar to that of Type 2 AGN. However, in contrast to Type 2 AGN, a high covering factor of the obscuring material, possibly sustained by inflows linked to the galaxy merger, and similar to that expected in deeply obscured compact obscured nuclei (CONs), is needed to explain the absence of extended high-ionization emission. Therefore, NGC 3256 S shares properties with CONs and Type 2 AGN.

papers.title: Latest $$s from the Earliest Galaxies: Probing neutrino self-interactions with JWST
papers.abstract: Our Universe serves as a complementary laboratory for particle physics interactions. One intriguing possibility is that neutrinos may have beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) self-interactions, which can delay their free streaming and have an observable effect across different redshifts. Such interactions can induce scale-dependent changes in the matter power spectrum. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has opened up a new window onto the early Universe by discovering a large population of high-redshift galaxies up to $z \sim 15$ and various probable galaxy candidates at even higher redshifts, between $z \sim 15-30$. Such high-redshift observations can probe the matter power spectrum on small scales, since structure formation is hierarchical and the structures hosting these high-redshift galaxies are therefore expected to be small. We, $\textit{for the first time}$, use the UV luminosity function data from JWST and combine them with the $\textit{Planck}$ CMB data to probe neutrino self-interactions ($\nu$SI). If only one neutrino flavor experiences such BSM interactions, then $\textit{Planck}$ + JWST data give a 95% C.L. upper limit on $\mathrm{Log}_{10}(G_{\mathrm{eff}}/\mathrm{MeV}^{-2})$ $\approx$ $-2.75$ and when all three flavors are interacting, the corresponding constraint becomes $\lesssim -3.41$; both stronger than those obtained using only $\textit{Planck}$ data. Our results highlight the power of this new observable, the high-redshift UV luminosity function from JWST as a complementary probe to terrestrial experiments, showing that small-scale observables can open a new window onto smaller neutrino self-interaction strengths.

papers.title: Constraining the spectral gap of 2d CFTs just above c=1
papers.abstract: We numerically study the space of compact unitary two-dimensional conformal field theories (2d CFTs) with central charge $c>1$ using the modular bootstrap. We focus on bounding the spectral gap $\Delta_{\rm gap}$ of such theories, namely the smallest scaling dimension among the non-vacuum primary operators. We use both a primal method that directly searches for consistent spectra and a dual method that yields rigorous exclusions. A key feature of our analysis is requiring the degeneracies of primary operators to be positive integers. At $c$ very near $1$, the integrality constraint greatly reduces the allowed spectral gap in both methods. For example, at $c-1 = 3\times 10^{-3}$ integrality strengthens the rigorous bound from $\Delta_{\rm gap} \lesssim 0.5$ to $\Delta_{\rm gap} < 0.041$. Our results suggest that the spectral gap might vanish as $c$ approaches $1$ from above.

papers.title: Probing Dark Matter-Electron Scattering with the Central Molecular Zone
papers.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone, a dense and gas-rich region surrounding the Galactic Center, hosts numerous dense molecular gas cores that provide unique environments to probe dark matter interactions. Among these, the IRS 13E3 cluster is one of the closest to the Galactic Center and one of the most extensively studied. We show that dark matter-electron scattering can substantially ionize molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) in the IRS 13E3 core, contributing to the ionization rate in conjunction with standard cosmic rays. Using the ionization rate inferred from H$_3^+$ observations of the central parsecs, we derive constraints on heavy and ultralight dark photon mediators, a heavy leptophilic mediator, and electric dipole moment interactions in the strongly interacting regime, where terrestrial searches are limited by the overburden problem. Our results highlight the potential of dense molecular cores near the Galactic Center as promising targets for constraining dark matter interactions with future observations.

papers.title: Black Hole Seeds and Little Red Dots: Connecting Formation and Growth with a JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury Program
papers.abstract: JWST has revealed an abundant population of faint active galactic nuclei and a new class of compact, high-redshift sources known as Little Red Dots (LRDs), whose physical nature remains debated, with accreting massive black holes among the leading explanations. The emerging demographics of early black holes, with their high inferred number densities and, in some systems, the apparent excess of black hole mass relative to stellar mass, challenge simple scenarios of black hole seeding and growth. Despite these observational breakthroughs, the origin of early massive black holes remains uncertain, because "black holes have no memory": current samples cannot separate the imprint of seeding from subsequent growth. This white paper identifies the multi-cycle JWST observations needed to revolutionize our understanding of early black hole growth by: (i) distinguishing seeding pathways, (ii) constraining early black hole growth mechanisms, (iii) resolving the physical nature of broad-line emitters and LRDs, and (iv) testing black hole-galaxy co-evolution. These tasks require uniformly selected samples extending to low black hole and host-galaxy masses, allowing self-consistent measurements of black hole mass functions, Eddington-ratio distributions, and host properties. Grating spectroscopy, deep MIRI imaging, and variability analysis through repeated observations of the same fields would provide complementary tests of black hole formation and growth, their connection to host-galaxy evolution, and the nature of newly discovered populations of LRDs. In this white paper, we argue that these joint tests require a coordinated JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury program; such a program could provide the depth, uniformity, and time baseline needed to place substantially stronger, complementary constraints on early black hole formation, growth, and their connection to galaxy evolution.

papers.title: SHARP(ening the) view of unresolved globular clusters in ultra diffuse galaxies
papers.abstract: Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies (UDGs) challenge current galaxy formation models within the {\Lambda}CDM framework, particularly regarding their dark matter content and formation histories. Globular Clusters (GCs) serve as excellent tracers for probing the halos of these faint systems; however, current spectroscopic facilities struggle to reach the depth required to fully characterize GC populations beyond the local neighborhood. In this work, we present the scientific potential of NEXUS@SHARP, a near-infrared multi-slit spectrograph proposed on the upcoming Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). We demonstrate that NEXUS is uniquely positioned to overcome current observational limitations by combining high spatial resolution with efficient multiplexing. We show that NEXUS can efficiently help to characterize the GC population in UDGs across diverse environments out to 60 to 70 Mpc - with a few hours of ELT time. These capabilities will allow for precise measurements of radial velocities and stellar populations, enabling robust dynamical mass estimates and distinguishing between competing UDG formation scenario.

papers.title: Unveiling the Origins of Local Group Galaxies with ELT-SHARP: An Overview of Science Cases
papers.abstract: The $\Lambda$CDM paradigm successfully describes large-scale cosmic structure, yet tensions possibly persist on galactic and sub-galactic scales. The Milky Way and the Local Universe offer a uniquely accessible laboratory to probe these discrepancies through chemo-dynamical studies of resolved stellar populations. Understanding disk assembly, dynamical heating, and galactoseismology requires wide-field coverage and high-angular-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy capable of penetrating dust-obscured regions and resolving crowded stellar environments. We propose science cases exploiting \textsc{SHARP}, a multi-mode near-infrared spectrograph for Extremely Large Telescopes and future space facilities. Operating over $0.95$--$2.45\,\mu$m in a single exposure, \textsc{SHARP} enables efficient access to key stellar and gas tracers across the Galactic bulge, disk, halo, and nearby galaxies. The \textsc{NEXUS} mode provides adaptive-optics-assisted multi-object spectroscopy over a $1.2'\times1.2'$ field with spectral resolutions up to $R\sim17{,}000$, enabling gas and stellar kinematics. Complementarily, the \textsc{VESPER} multi-IFU mode delivers spatially resolved spectroscopy in crowded regions, allowing reconstruction of internal kinematics and stellar population gradients on sub-arcsecond scales. Combined with surveys such as \textit{Gaia}, APOGEE, LAMOST, LSST, 4MOST, and ELT--MOSAIC, this project will map six-dimensional phase-space structures of disk and bulge stars, stellar streams, and nearby disk galaxies (e.g. LMC, SMC). The data will enable investigations of bars, spiral arms, warps, flares, and satellite interactions, providing critical constraints on disk evolution, merger history, and dark matter substructure, and providing stringent tests of $\Lambda$CDM on the smallest accessible scales.
